cases.title: Review provider and model apply to reviewers only
steps: Build the engine and make a fresh temp repo as TESTING.md 'How to see the app' describes ($CLI, $FIX, $REPO)
cd $REPO && node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider fake --review-provider fake --review-model rm1; echo EXIT=$?
cat $REPO/.graph-execution/<run-id>/state.json; ls $REPO/.graph-execution/<run-id>/
node $CLI --resume --review-provider fake; echo EXIT=$?
node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider fake --review-provider nope; echo EXIT=$?
cases.expected: EXIT=0; state.json has "reviewProvider":"fake" and "reviewModel":"rm1"; the run dir has no reviewers.json; the resume prints '--review-provider cannot be used with --resume; the run keeps the review provider it started with' and EXIT=2; 'nope' gives EXIT=2 listing the providers

cases.title: New providers are listed and checked at startup
steps: Build the engine and make a fresh temp repo as TESTING.md 'How to see the app' describes ($CLI, $FIX, $REPO)
node $CLI --help
cd $REPO && PATH=$(dirname $(command -v node)):$(dirname $(command -v git)) node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider pi; echo EXIT=$?
same with --provider copilot and --provider omp
cases.expected: --help lists claude|codex|opencode|qwen|pi|omp|copilot; each run exits 2 with 'the "<bin>" CLI was not found on the PATH' (omp may instead say it needs Bun), and no .graph-execution folder is created

cases.title: Sandbox commands work without Docker where they should
steps: Build the engine and make a fresh temp repo as TESTING.md 'How to see the app' describes ($CLI, $FIX, $REPO)
cd $REPO && node $CLI sandbox dockerfile --provider claude --provider omp
node $CLI sandbox config --base node:22-bookworm --line 'RUN echo hi'; cat graph-execution.config.json
node $CLI sandbox config --line 'FROM x'; echo EXIT=$?
PATH=$(dirname $(command -v node)):$(dirname $(command -v git)) node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider fake --sandbox; echo EXIT=$?
cases.expected: the Dockerfile starts 'FROM node:24.22.1-bookworm', installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code, @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent and bun, and prints '# tag: graph-execution-sandbox:<12 hex>'; the config file has {"sandbox":{"base":"node:22-bookworm","dockerfile":["RUN echo hi"]}}; the FROM line gives EXIT=2 and leaves the file unchanged; the run without docker exits 2 with '--sandbox needs Docker' and creates no run

cases.title: A sandboxed run with the fake docker in exec mode reaches applied and its page opens with the token
steps: Build the engine and make a fresh temp repo as TESTING.md 'How to see the app' describes ($CLI, $FIX, $REPO)
Put the test fake docker (packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/fake-docker.ts, built to dist or run with the same helper the tests use) on PATH in exec mode as its header comment describes
cd $REPO && SSH_CONNECTION=1 node $CLI $FIX/diamond --spec $FIX/spec.md --provider fake --sandbox; echo EXIT=$?
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' '<printed url>' ; curl -s -c jar -L '<printed url>' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'; curl -s -b jar http://127.0.0.1:<port>/state
node $CLI list; cat .graph-execution/<run-id>/sandbox.json
cases.expected: EXIT=0 and 'Run <id> started in a sandbox: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=…'; the first curl is 302, following it with the cookie gives 200 and /state answers JSON; a request without token or cookie is 401; list shows the run (sandbox ge-sbx-<id>); sandbox.json has container, url and token; the run reaches applied

cases.title: Start run has review provider fields and agent-opened animation
steps: Start graph-manager as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes, log in, connect the fake forge and clone octo/hello
agent-browser: Runs -> Start run; screenshot; pick Review provider 'codex', type 'o3' in Review model; read the command preview; close

In a terminal opened in octo/hello, have the MCP tool open_start_run called (e.g. run graph-manager-mcp by hand as TESTING.md 'Terminals' shows, or call POST /api/internal tool route the tests use) with tasksDir diamond and spec spec.md while that terminal is on screen; screenshot during the first 400 ms and after 2 s
cases.expected: The form shows 'Review provider' (default 'Same as run') and 'Review model'; the preview contains '--review-provider codex --review-model o3'; the agent-opened drawer has class drawer-agent, slides in from the right edge with a glow and shows the badge 'Opened by Claude Code' (or the agent's label) with its icon; the button-opened drawer has no badge

cases.title: New agents in graph-manager terminals
steps: Start graph-manager as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes with fake bins named pi, omp and copilot on its PATH
curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/agents
Open a Copilot, an oh-my-pi and a pi terminal from the Terminals sidebar; read the typed command line in each
ls $GM_DIR/data/agents; cat $HOME/.omp/agent/mcp.json (with the server's HOME)
cases.expected: /api/agents lists 7 agents (copilot inject, omp user-config, pi extension); the terminals type 'copilot --additional-mcp-config @…/agents/copilot-mcp.json', 'omp' and 'pi -e …/agents/pi-graph-manager.ts'; both agent files exist; ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json has mcpServers.graph-manager

cases.title: Terminals run graph-manager's engine and agents get the skills
steps: Start graph-manager as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes with a temp HOME
ls $HOME/.pi/agent/skills $HOME/.copilot/skills $HOME/.omp/agent/skills $HOME/.claude/skills

In a graph-manager terminal: env | grep -E 'GM_ENGINE_BIN|GRAPH_EXECUTION_DELEGATE'; then run another copy of the engine (e.g. node <a copy of dist/cli.js> --version) and compare with graph-manager's engine version
curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/health; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7420/healthz; open Settings and screenshot the Engine card
cases.expected: each skills folder has to-spec, to-tasks and run-graph; both env vars are set; the copy delegates and prints graph-manager's engine version; /api/health has engine {bin, version}; /healthz is {"ok":true}; Settings shows the engine version

cases.title: install skills per agent
steps: Build the engine and make a fresh temp repo as TESTING.md 'How to see the app' describes ($CLI, $FIX, $REPO)
cd $REPO && node $CLI install skills --target pi && node $CLI install skills --target all --force && find . -name SKILL.md -path '*skills*' | sort
node $CLI install skills --target nope; echo EXIT=$?
cases.expected: .pi/skills, .github/skills, .omp/skills, .qwen/skills, .opencode/skills, .claude/skills and .agents/skills each contain to-spec, to-tasks and run-graph; the unknown target gives EXIT=2 listing the targets
